role: Director, Ohio Department of Natural Resources
summary: William B. Nye, Director of the Ohio Department of Natural Resources, found the draft environmental impact statement to be an excellent and thorough product and recommended that the Department of Interior proceed with its finalization. He conditionally supported the proposal, urging that mechanisms be developed for ORV site selection that minimize adverse impacts and irretrievable resource loss, and that qualified personnel periodically inspect areas in use. He also suggested that a public land use plan could help facilitate site selections that protect unique natural areas, special soil and vegetative conditions, and wildlife habitat.

statement.text:
WILLIAM B. NYE DIRECTOR
DEPARTMENT OF MATURAL RESOURCES
OHIO DEPARTMENTS BUILDING COLUMEUS 43215
August 9, 1972
United States Department of Interior Bureau of Outdoor Recreation Washington, D.C. 20240 Attn: G. Douglas Hofe, Jr., Director
Draft Environmental Impact RE: Statement for Implementation of Executive Order 11644-Use of Off-Road Vehicles on Public
Lands-Kl4
Dear Director Hofe:
In response to your letter of June 1, 1972 forwarding the draft environmental impact statement for the above referenced project, a review was coordinated by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources. Comments were solicited from other State agencies under the auspices of the Office of the Governor, State Clearinghouse.
This draft environmental impact statement is an excellent, well-thought product. It is thorough and easily understood. We have no comments on the five points.
The Department of Interior should proceed with finalization of the statement. We would, however, urge you to promote mechanisms for site selection for Off-Road Vehicles use which would allow for the least adverse impact and irretrievable loss in the area being considered. In addition, qualified personnel should periodically inspect areas in use to assess the deterioration of existing land forms.
In light of the fact that ORV site selections must take into account the preservation of unique natural areas, special soil and vegetative conditions, wildlife habitat areas, etc., perhaps the implementation of a public land use plan would aid and/or facilitate these selections.

Director G. Douglas Hofe, Jr. August 9, 1972 Page Two
Thank you for the opportunity to review and comment on the impact statement. We look forward to receiving the final form and to cooperation in any way with the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation personnel associated with the State of Ohio in implementing this Executive Order.
Sincerely,
WILLIAM B. NYE Director
